value.body: An ergonomics consultant studies how people sit, lift and work, and suggests changes to reduce aches, strain and injury. Employers include corporate wellness and occupational-health providers, large offices, factories and warehouses. A day may include workstation assessments, short training sessions and follow-ups with employees who have complaints.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BPT, often with a certificate in ergonomics or occupational health

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Posture and workstation checklists, risk-assessment methods, basic measurement tools

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Most BPT graduates first gain some clinical experience, then move into corporate wellness or occupational-health providers. A short ergonomics certification and experience with musculoskeletal conditions make applications stronger.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Teaching posture and exercise to groups

value.title: At a glance
items: A niche field; openings are fewer than in clinical physiotherapy.
Next roles: senior ergonomist, occupational health lead, or independent consulting.
Some roles combine ergonomics with general on-site physiotherapy.
